match.reason: No point in the bank covers resolving workplace disputes through negotiation, mediation, grievance procedures or the Fair Work Commission, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Resolving disputes
card: Negotiation
The two sides talk directly and try to reach an agreement themselves. No outside person is involved.
Mediation
A neutral third party helps both sides talk and find a solution. The mediator does not make the decision.
Grievance procedure
A set of steps in a business that an employee follows to raise a complaint. It usually starts with the supervisor and can move up to senior managers.
Fair Work Commission
If these steps fail, the Commission can step in. It may conciliate, by helping the parties reach agreement, or arbitrate, by making a decision that the parties must follow.
draft.remember: Settle it by talking first. Only when that fails does the Fair Work Commission step in.

a.q: Two sides in a dispute use a neutral person who helps them talk but cannot decide the outcome. What is this process?
a.why: A neutral third party who helps the sides reach their own solution is a mediator. Negotiation is similar, but it has no outside person, as the two sides talk directly.
a.clue: Look for the neutral helper who does not decide.

b.q: Priya's employer will not discuss her roster change. Talks with her manager failed. The Fair Work Commission now decides the outcome, and both sides must follow it. What process is this?
b.why: In arbitration the Commission makes a decision that the parties must follow. Conciliation is the tempting answer, but there the Commission only helps the parties reach their own agreement.
b.clue: Who makes the final decision in this case?

problems.detail: The remember line says "Only when that fails does the Fair Work Commission step in", but the card says the Commission "can" step in. "Only" makes the rule sound absolute when the card is softer.

"No outside person is involved" in negotiation can mislead. In Australian workplaces, representatives such as union officials often negotiate for employees. What negotiation lacks is a neutral third party. Better: "No neutral third party is involved."
The stem says Priya's employer "will not discuss" the roster change, then that "talks with her manager failed". These clash and may confuse students about whether talks happened at all.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer (Mediation, Arbitration). Fix three things: the remember line uses "only" where the card says "can", the card's "no outside person" overlooks union representatives in negotiation, and question b's stem is slightly contradictory.
